useDistrict.label: Zoning use district
useDistrict.method: The parcel’s acdm-wktn zoning_code (the active row of its map lot, the row whose lot is the map lot first), as the scenario step reads it; empty when it has none. A split code such as RH-1|RM-1 is kept whole.

historic.label: Historic resource status

sources.label: DataSF Historic Resource Status by Parcel

historic.method: The most protective ceqacodea10a11 of the parcel’s 3tsw-4idn rows, ranked A* > A > B > C, each row joined by apn to an active acdm-wktn blklot and its map lot; empty when the parcel has none (sd.historic.no-row, 4 / 4). Historic protection is A or A* (ruling 4).

exemptions.label: SB 79 exemptions (Ord. 082-26)

sources.label: SF Board File 260132 – SB 79 exemption tables (Ord. 082-26)

exemptions.method: The §3 Table of Permanent Exclusions and the §4 Table of Temporary Exemptions of Board File 260132, transcribed to pipeline/enrichment/sb79-exemptions.csv and checked against the originals’ sha256 at normalise. A parcel is exempt when one of its active blklots is listed; a row that matches no active parcel is dropped (sd.exempt.unmatched).

sb79.label: SB 79 as written

sources.label: MTC "Senate Bill 79 - Transit-Oriented Development Transit Stops", agency SFMTA, tod_tier "Tier 2", excluding planned (mtc:*) stops; stop_code matched to SFMTA Muni GTFS stops.txt stop_id

sb79.method: Gov. Code §65912.157 as written, ignoring the City’s exemptions and Density Bonus Law. TOD stops come from the GTFS feeds (tier source gtfs): heavy rail is tier 1, commuter rail tier 1 at 72 or more trains a day at the station and tier 2 at 48, light rail, streetcar and the Muni stops MTC designates current tier 2 (planned stops left out) tier 2. The band is the straight-line distance from the DataSF parcel outline to the nearest stop point of each tier (200 ft, ¼ mile, ½ mile); the tallest standard wins. Stories are 10 ft each of its height and the cap is its du/ac × lot acres, rounded up. The lot must be scenario-eligible, zoned residential, mixed or commercial, not hold more than 2 homes likely rent-controlled (built before 1979; occupancy not modelled), and yield at least 5 homes at full fill; fill levels below 5 are 0.

currentLaw.method: The FZP envelope, cap and yields of parcels.bin (the FZP yield cap is none on Local Program parcels and the base-zoning cap on 2026-10-10 elsewhere), raised by Planning Code §207.11 (Ord. 082-26 §5) where it applies. §207.11 applies within ½ mile of an SB 79 TOD stop (the SB 79 tiers and bands), on a scenario-eligible lot that is in neither Board File 260132 exemption table, zoned for principally permitted residential use, with a numeric density cap or a base height under 40 ft, outside R-4, not an Article 10 or 11 resource (historic status A*), and whose cap is below half the SB 79 density of its tier and band (Planning’s reading of (b)(8)); the density-bonus condition (b)(5) is not modelled. There a base height under 40 ft becomes 40 ft (4 stories) and the cap is the larger of the FZP cap and half the SB 79 density × lot acres, rounded half up. A lot takes §207.11 when its full-fill yield is larger and it can host a project; a tie keeps FZP.
